title: Inter-professional quality improvement project to reduce intensive care days in a multietiological intensive care unit. The contribution of Speech and Language Therapy to the overall result.
summary:
Patients who stay in intensive care for a long time often have serious illnesses and a higher risk of health problems and even death after treatment. A long stay in the intensive care unit also means that there are fewer beds available for other patients. Reasons for a long stay include, for example, if many organs are not functioning properly, the circulation is unstable, the patient is confused or weaning from the ventilator takes longer. A tracheal cannula can also mean that the patient has to stay longer because other wards or care facilities have difficulties with care.
Various disciplines are working together in a joint project to identify problems that prevent premature discharge from the intensive care unit. These include doctors, nursing staff, physiotherapists, speech therapists and occupational therapists. The speech therapists focus on the management of the tracheostomy tube and on training patients to swallow. Their aim is to remove the tube as quickly as possible if it is safe for the patient, or to help the patient to care for the tube themselves.
Two work instructions have been drawn up: one for patients who have difficulty swallowing and one for tracheostomy tube management. These instructions are based on recommendations from international experts and are to be gradually introduced in an intensive care unit providing post-surgery care in 2024. To check the effect of these measures, an analysis of data from 2022 and 2023 will be carried out. This data will serve as a comparison.
conditions: All tracheotomized patients between 2022 and 2023 with at least one day of stay in the general postoperative intensive care unit of the anesthesiology department.

interventions.name: Historical control. Retrospective analysis of health data for all tracheostomized patients between 2022 and 2023.
